script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - MORNING

JAMES SITTING ALONE AT A TABLE, laptop open in front of him. He looks exhausted, his eyes sunken and his face lined with worry.

WAITRESS approaches.

WAITRESS
(cheerfully)
Morning, sir. What can I get started for you today?

JAMES
(sighs)
Just a black coffee, please.

As the waitress walks away, JAMES's gaze lingers on a flyer in the window across the street. It's for a new startup company looking for talented programmers.

EXT. STARTUP OFFICE - DAY

James enters the office, feeling a sense of excitement and nervousness. He's wearing a suit, a departure from his usual t-shirt and jeans attire. He meets with the CEO, SARA, in her office.

SARA
(smiling)
Nice to meet you, James. I've heard great things about your programming skills.

JAMES
(nervously)
Thank you. I'm eager to start and learn new things.

SARA
(laughs)
That's the spirit! We have a challenging project coming up, and I believe you'll fit in perfectly.

INT. JAMES'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

James sits on his couch, staring at the laptop screen. His mind is racing with new ideas and challenges. He's excited about this new opportunity, but the weight of the responsibility is heavy on his shoulders.

Suddenly, his phone rings. It's his ex-boss, RICHARD, from his old job.

RICHARD
(angrily)
I can't believe you left without a fight. You were one of our top programmers, James. I thought you had more ambition than that.

JAMES
(calmly)
I've made my decision, Richard. I believe this new opportunity is the best thing for me.

RICHARD
(scoffs)
Suit yourself. Don't expect me to help you out if you ever find yourself in a bind.

James hangs up the phone, feeling a pang of regret. But he knows he made the right decision.

EXT. PARK - DAY

James takes a break from work and goes for a walk in the park. He sees a woman, MIA, playing the piano in a gazebo. She's lost in the music, her fingers dancing over the keys with grace and precision.

MIA
(smiling)
Hello there. Care for a listen?

JAMES
(surprised)
I'd love to. You're very talented.

MIA
(laughs)
Thank you. Music has a way of soothing the soul.

They strike up a conversation, and James finds himself opening up to her in a way he hasn't been able to with anyone else. They talk about their dreams and aspirations, and James realizes that he's not alone in his journey.

INT. JAMES'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

James is back at home, still feeling overwhelmed by the new job. He looks at the flyer from the coffee shop window, remembering the excitement he felt when he first saw it. He picks up the phone and calls Mia.

MIA
(answering)
Hello, James.

JAMES
(hesitantly)
Hi, Mia. I was wondering if you'd like to have dinner with me sometime. I could use someone to talk to about this new opportunity.

MIA
(smiling)
Of course, James. I'd be happy to.

EXT. ITALIAN RESTAURANT - EVENING

James and Mia sit in a cozy Italian restaurant, surrounded by twinkling fairy lights and the sound of laughter. They talk about their dreams and fears, and James realizes that he's not the only one struggling with the weight of responsibility.

MIA
(seriously)
You know, James, it's important to remember that it's okay to ask for help. We all have our moments of doubt and fear.

JAMES
(nodding)
I know. It's just hard to let go of that feeling of needing to do it all on my own.

MIA
(smiling)
Well, you don't have to do it alone. I'm here for you, and so are the people at your new job.

James smiles, feeling a sense of relief wash over him. He realizes that this new opportunity is not just about his career, but also about learning to trust and rely on others.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
